SEC 13F ingestion · live filing season

The Q3 2026 filing season so far: parsed, identified, and checked against what changed later.

Every 13F filed with the SEC from 1 Oct – 15 Oct 2026, while funds report their 30 September positions. Every number below was measured by a script you can run.

10 steps, about two minutes

The season so far

1,224 13F filings, 1 Oct – 15 Oct 2026
1,224 parsed here — all of them
275,045 holdings parsed
25,426 holdings per second
216.43 ms largest single filing

Funds have 45 days after the quarter ends to file, so this is the early part of the Q3 2026 season: 1,148 of these filings report the quarter ending 2026-09-30. The biggest — Farther Finance Advisors, LLC, 6,201 holdings — took 216.43 ms. We report throughput rather than an average per filing because filing sizes are wildly uneven: the median filing holds just 102 positions. Cost is about 39.3 microseconds per holding. Timing covers document to structured rows; it excludes network time, which is the SEC's to control, not ours.

Inside one filing

CompanyCUSIPTickerFIGIISIN ValueStatus

The CUSIP is what the filing gives you. Everything to its right we added, from free sources.

Identifier resolution, including what fails

10,320 distinct identifiers
92.2% resolved to a FIGI
31 unresolved in the sample
5.9% non-US identifiers
0 SEDOLs — licensed

Sources: OpenFIGI for FIGI and ticker, and a derived ISIN for US securities. No licence, no contract, no vendor fee. The rate is measured on a random sample of 399 of the 10,320 distinct identifiers, deliberately not on the largest holdings — those are well-known US securities and would flatter the figure. Most failures are non-US securities, which the free sources do not carry. SEDOL is licensed by LSEG and cannot be supplied this way; our proposal offered it, and that needs correcting.

What happens after a filing is published

A filing is not final. Firms return months or years later and change what they already reported. There is no corrections feed, no notification, and nothing in the new document says which filing it replaces.

36 corrections, 1 Oct – 15 Oct 2026
34 published quarters changed
7 arrived 90+ days late
9.5 yrs furthest reach back

Blackstone Inc. — quarter ending 2026-06-30

Filed 2026-08-14
557 holdings
→
Corrected 2026-10-09
2 holdings

The correction says new holdings — add these, keep the rest. Handle it as a replacement, which is the obvious default, and $32.9bn of holdings disappear 56 days after they were first reported.

Across the window: assuming corrections replace wrongly deletes $85.1bn; assuming they add wrongly double-counts $17.7bn. One field decides which, and 0.0% of corrections do not state it at all.

What this demonstrates

  • Ingestion is fast and provably so — 275,045 holdings across 1,224 filings in 10,818 ms, about 39.3 microseconds per holding.
  • Identifiers resolve at 92.2% from free sources on a random sample, with the failures published rather than rounded away — and SEDOL, which our proposal promised, cannot be delivered without a licence.
  • The hard part is time, not parsing. Holdings history is rewritten after publication. A store that records only which quarter a fact belongs to — and not when it was learned — is wrong and cannot tell you so.
  • No AI was used anywhere in this pipeline. The filings are structured XML. Adding a model would add cost and risk without adding accuracy.

Method. All 1,224 13F-HR filings accepted by SEC EDGAR from 1 Oct – 15 Oct 2026, downloaded and parsed (1,224 carried a holdings table). Identifiers resolved via OpenFIGI. Corrections cover all 36 13F-HR/A filings in the same window, each matched to the filing it corrects; 0 had no retrievable original and are excluded from the dollar figures. Generated 2026-10-16.

Limits. The Q3 2026 season is still open until 14 November, so these are the early filers. US filings only. 13F covers long US-listed equity — no shorts, no non-US listings, no bonds. Amendment chains are not modelled. The value figures are gross exposure under each wrong rule, not realised loss.

Public SEC data throughout. Every figure regenerates from source with uv run pipeline.py and uv run build.py.
